anti_overlap: Property-graph and RDF modelling, reification patterns, label/index design as ontology, Zod and loader syntax — owned by the graph-ontology reviewer. This lens owns the medium's physics (where a cord is tied, what an empty register means, what a record costs to write), not type systems or modelling correctness.

Correlation estimation mechanics, measurement invariance, factor structure, and pairwise deletion as statistical craft — owned by the psychometrics reviewer. This lens owns exact reconciliation of group totals, not inference from a sample; where it touches an estimator it must speak arithmetically, not inferentially.

Archetype theory, sign/object/interpretant analysis, motif-index classification, and whether a symbol row denotes one coherent referent — owned by the semiotics reviewer. This lens owns only the fact that the record cannot supply a referent and needs an external reader to.

Chain-of-transmission grading, corroboration counting, common-link analysis, and whether 2+ sources is a defensible evidentiary bar — owned by the transmission-criticism reviewer. Cede all of it; raise only the narrow point that duplicate records are independent by custody of separate objects, not by differing content.
Reference frames, moving or invisible reference objects, blurred versus point placement, and coordinate-free position as a navigation question — owned by the wayfinding reviewer.
Load paths, thrust lines, joints, differential settlement, build sequencing, temporary works, and irreversibility as curing — owned by the masonry reviewer.

Substrate affinity, concentration per bath, cross-staining, metamerism, and the mordant/resist framings of coordinate-free symbols — owned by the dyeing reviewer. Where this lens also arrives at 'no numbers', it must arrive by attachment point and second channel, or say nothing.
Copyright, paraphrase practice, site presentation, and UX — out of scope here.
decision_lens: Trace the knot to the total. For any claim that symbols do or do not affect an estimate, name the physical attachment (label, collection, file, index) that enrolls the record, and refuse any exclusion that rests on a convention rather than on where the cord is tied. Before arguing about values, separate the three absences — zero, no-register, never-tied — and check what the reading code writes when it meets each. Prefer a shorter cord over an empty register, prefer the categorical channel over an unearned number, and sum only within a group. Then ask who reads it: an archive with no keeper is not a cheap archive, it is not an archive.
distance_rationale: The seven lenses already on this question own representation (ontology), estimation (psychometrics), meaning (semiotics), reference frames (etak), transmission provenance (isnād), force and sequence (masonry), and affinity and concentration (dyeing). None of them owns THE MEDIUM OF RECORD ITSELF: what a physical registry can be made to say, what an absence looks like on it, what a record costs to tie, which totals a given entry is structurally enrolled in, and what the archive is worth when the person who could read it is gone. Khipu is that discipline and nothing else in the set is. Its primitives are attachment point, register position, knotless space, group spacing, ply direction, colour channel, top-cord sum, and the cord-keeper — none shared with statistics, textual criticism, structural statics, dye chemistry, graph modelling, mythology, or navigation. It is pre-modern, Andean, non-Western, and not remotely an AI-cliché domain. (The dyer lens's domain string mentions Andean cochineal; that is a geographic coincidence with zero shared primitives — dyeing is the chemistry of what happens in one vessel, khipu is the arithmetic and legibility of a tallied archive.) It earns its seat on this specific document because the repo's own code contains khipu problems the other lenses cannot name. (1) buildGraph.ts:143-151 imputes the corpus mean for every not-applicable axis into a fixed-width 29-float cosine index — the medium has no way to write 'no claim', so a knotless space is read as a definite value. Khipu is the only tradition in the set whose central notational fact is that zero is an absence at an expected position, distinguishable from a cord that has no such register and from a cord never tied at all. (2) That axisMean is computed over `creatures`; if symbols take the Creature label they move the mean that supplies their own filler — a top cord summing pendants whose values were read off the top cord. (3) Top cords sum only their own pendant group and never across groups of different colour, which is a sharper statement of the sample-composition problem than 'more rows' — and it is a reconciliation rule, not an estimator's property. (4) Subsidiary cords hang off pendants and are never in the top-cord sum: that is a structurally-enforced unlisted option — a symbol recorded in full, located hierarchically, and outside every total BY ATTACHMENT rather than by a README convention — distinct from Option A's peer node, from reification, from the dyer's mordant/resist, and from etak's coordinate-free reckoning. (5) The categorical channel (colour, ply, attachment) carries real information with no knots at all, which is the version of the symbol tier that holds no numbers anywhere. (6) The khipukamayuq is the exact shape of the confirmed finding that 99.6% of class:symbol rows still carry gloss: null: the Spanish inherited warehouses of arithmetically perfect cords nobody could read. No other lens here treats readability as a staffed office with a named holder and a failure state.
expected_isomorphisms: Zero written as a knotless space at an expected register ↔ buildGraph.ts:143-151's mean-imputation policy. The khipu reader knows a knotless space is a value (zero) and knows it only because the cord still has that register; the repo's 29-float cosine index likewise cannot hold 'no claim', so it writes the corpus mean. Under Option A or B every symbol receives the BEING corpus's mean on 24 of 29 dimensions — not a neutral filler but a confident statement that symbols sit at the centre of the being cloud.

The top cord that sums its pendant group, computed from cords that hang below it ↔ axisMean computed over `creatures`. If symbols carry the Creature label, the mean imputed into symbols is computed from a population that includes symbols — the sum is taken over cords whose values were read off the sum. A khipukamayuq would call this an untied archive; no statistical lens on this question has named the loop.

Level set by attachment point — a cord tied to the primary is a pendant and enters the group total; the identical cord tied to a pendant is subsidiary and does not ↔ the confirmed finding that the creatureEidogen vector index is keyed to the `:Creature` label rather than to a settable flag. Enrollment in a total is a physical fact about where the cord is knotted, never a rule written elsewhere. Every option must name its knot.

Subsidiary cords: full detail, hierarchically located, structurally excluded from the top-cord sum ↔ the unlisted Option E this lens owns — symbols attached beneath being entries rather than beside them. It gives the archetypal register somewhere to live, keeps the 546 pendant totals untouched by construction, and needs no convention to hold, because a subsidiary is not summed no matter who writes the next script.

The categorical channel — colour, barber-pole patterning, S/Z ply, recto/verso attachment — carrying category with zero knots ↔ a symbol tier that stores no numeric vector at all and is still fully expressive. This is a different route to coordinate-freedom than the dyer's resist (defined by exclusion) or etak's reference frames (defined by relative position): here the information is carried in a second channel of the same object, alongside a quantitative channel that is simply left untied.

Group boundaries made by spacing along the primary cord, and the rule that you never sum across groups of different colour ↔ the covariance census, the 47-family clustering, and relatedness V as group totals. The correct output is three reconciled figures (beings, symbols, pooled) with the pooled one explicitly labelled as crossing a group boundary — not one number over a corpus that has quietly become two populations.

The khipukamayuq, without whom the cords are arithmetically valid and semantically mute ↔ 99.6% of class:symbol rows and 99.9% of the promotion-eligible subset carrying gloss: null. Readability is a staffed office with a named holder, a cadence, and a documented failure state; the Spanish colonial archive is what an unstaffed one looks like. No option currently names a keeper for the symbol tier.

Matched-pair khipu — two cords of one tribute event held by two parties, where independence is guaranteed by custody of separate objects, not by their contents ↔ the '2+ independent sources' promotion bar. Two headwords inside one comparative symbol dictionary are one cord read twice, not a matched pair; the check that matters is who held the object, not whether the strings differ.

Inserting a pendant into a group shifts the position of every cord after it, so the same knots now read at different registers ↔ the measured V=801→796 precedent where a 0.6% change to the shared vocabulary universe flipped 13 creatures to orphan status. Insertion into a positional medium is never additive-only; the cost falls on records that never touched the new material.

Every knot is tied by hand and a register that must be present and empty still costs its length of cord ↔ the ~22,848 mandatory justification strings that any full-29-key option prices in for not-applicable axes. The khipu answer is not to tie an empty register more cheaply but to tie a SHORTER CORD — a record shape with fewer registers, which is a design choice about the medium rather than an authoring-effort optimisation.

An archive whose cords are all one colour and all tied at the same register loses the ability to distinguish its groups ↔ the confirmed heterogeneity of class:symbol (2,604 kind:archetype alongside 89 kind:individual and 5 kind:species). A khipukamayuq would refuse to tie individuated named objects, zodiacal signs, and generic archetypes onto one primary without spacing and colour distinguishing the groups.
focus: Whether each option can physically write what it claims to write: how an absence is recorded and how it is read back, which totals a symbol entry is enrolled in by its attachment point rather than by convention, what the record costs to tie, whether the quantitative channel is needed at all, and who is on staff to read the archive once it exists.
name: fd-khipu-cord-registry
persona: Apply the perspective of a khipukamayuq — a cord-keeper responsible for an archive that must reconcile. It thinks first about where a cord is tied, because that decides which total it enters; then about registers, because a knotless space is a value and a missing register is not; then about the second channel of colour and ply that carries category with no knots at all; then about the group spacing that keeps unlike things from being summed together. It knows the cords cannot say who they are about, and that an archive without its keeper is warehouse fibre.
review_areas: The typology of absence on the medium: separate zero (a knotless space at a register that exists), no-register (a shorter cord), and never-tied (no cord at all). Test each option against the repo's single not-applicable sentinel and against what each reading path actually writes when it meets one.

What the reader writes where the record is silent: buildGraph.ts:143-151 imputes the corpus mean into the fixed-width 29-float cosine index. State, per option, how many symbol records receive an imputed value on how many axes, and what the vector index then believes about them.

Imputation circularity: axisMean is computed over `creatures`. Say for each option whether symbols are inside that population, and if so, show the loop — a filler derived from a mean the filled records themselves move — and what closes it.

Centroid collapse: any option giving symbols 24 not-applicable axes inside a 29-dimension cosine index puts every symbol at the being-corpus centre in 24 of 29 dimensions. Work out what that does to personality-neighbour queries for the 546 BEINGS, not just for symbols.

Attachment, not convention: for each option, name the physical thing (Neo4j label, collection file, index membership, gate packet) that puts a symbol into or out of the covariance population, relatedness V, the 47-family clustering, and the vector index. Flag any exclusion that lives only in prose.

The subsidiary-cord option (unlisted): symbols recorded beneath being entries rather than beside them — full detail, hierarchically located, outside every group total by attachment. Develop it far enough to keep or kill: where it is stored, who loads it, what it cannot express, and how a symbol shared by twelve beings is handled.

The categorical-channel option: colour, ply and attachment carry information with no knots. Develop the symbol tier that stores no numeric vector anywhere and test whether it actually serves the Jungian/archetypal register the owner wants, or only avoids the ratchet.

Sum within a group, never across: require every option to state the covariance figures, family assignment, and relatedness V as three reconciled quantities (beings, symbols, pooled), and to mark the pooled figure explicitly as crossing a group boundary.

The cord-keeper: 99.6% of class:symbol rows and 99.9% of the promotion-eligible subset carry gloss: null. Name the keeper for the symbol tier — who writes and maintains the gloss, on what cadence — and describe the failure state of an archive tied with no keeper.

Cost is per knot and per cord: price each option in records actually tied, counting registers that must be present and empty (the mandatory not-applicable justification prose). Where the price is the empty registers, ask what a shorter cord would look like instead of asking for cheaper knots.

Insertion renumbers: adding cords to a positional medium re-reads what was already there. Trace, per option, what changes for the 546 existing beings after the symbol records land — the measured V=801→796 orphan flip is the shape to test against, not a worst case.

severity_examples.condition: When an option places symbols inside any population whose own summary statistic is used to fill values on those same symbols, or places records with mostly-absent registers into a fixed-width index whose reader substitutes a value for absence.
severity_examples.scenario: The knotless space is read as a number, and the number is circular. Symbols take the Creature label (the easy way to make them resolve as relation targets), so all ~952 enter buildGraph.ts's creatureEidogen index. Each carries real values on the five universal axes and the not-applicable sentinel on the other 24, so the imputation policy writes the corpus mean into 24 of 29 dimensions for every symbol — and axisMean is itself computed over the population that now includes those symbols. Every symbol lands within a hair of every other symbol and at the exact centre of the being cloud; personality-neighbour queries for the 546 beings return a wall of symbols before they return any creature, and the mean that produced them is partly a function of them. The archive reconciles to a total that includes cords whose values were read off the total.

severity_examples.condition: When an option ships symbol records whose readability depends on a gloss, provenance note, or interpretation that no named person, script, or cadence is responsible for producing — and when nothing in the load path fails if it is missing.
severity_examples.scenario: An archive tied with no keeper. 952 symbol entries are promoted with a vector, a graph node, and citations — and with gloss: null carried straight through from the registry, because nothing in the promotion path requires a gloss and no one owns writing them. The cords are arithmetically valid: validateCanon passes, the covariance gate passes, the site renders. But no consumer can say what any given symbol entry is about, the jawnsight grammar (which validates nothing about the payload it reads) derives player-visible traits from records with no readable referent, and the citation-stability rule means these entries can never be replaced, only amended. This is exactly the Spanish colonial inheritance: warehouses of perfect cords and nobody left who could read them.

severity_examples.condition: When an option admits symbols into a shared estimate without requiring that estimate to be reported per group, or when a baseline is re-stamped over a corpus whose composition changed in the same batch.
severity_examples.scenario: Sums taken across group boundaries. The covariance report, the 47-family clustering, and relatedness V each continue to emit one figure over a corpus that has become two populations with different register coverage. The pooled max |r| moves, and nobody can say whether it moved because a being pair got more collinear or because 952 records with five registers each were spaced onto the same primary cord. The ratchet then stamps the pooled figure as the new baseline, and the group boundary is lost permanently — no later reading can decompose it back.

source_domain: Inka khipu cord-record keeping (Andean, c. 1400–1600, and its colonial-era administration) — the knotted-cord archive as a physical recording medium: a primary cord carrying pendant cords, subsidiary cords hanging off pendants, and top cords holding the sum of the pendant group they crown; base-10 positional knotting read by distance along the cord (clustered single knots for higher registers, a long knot for units, a figure-eight for one), with zero written as a knotless space at the expected register rather than by any mark of its own; a wholly separate categorical channel that carries no quantity at all — cord colour and barber-pole colour patterning, S- versus Z-ply spin direction, recto/verso attachment, and group boundaries made by spacing along the primary; hierarchy expressed by where a cord is tied rather than by what it records; matched-pair khipu of one event held by two different parties as a custody-based duplication check; and the khipukamayuq, the cord-keeper whose oral gloss the archive cannot be read without — a record fully determinate in its arithmetic and radically under-determined in its referents.
success_hints: Separate the three absences before arguing about any value — 'this is a knotless space being read as a confident number' is a sharper and more actionable finding than 'the sentinel is overloaded'.
Follow the knot to the total: never assert that symbols do or don't touch an estimate without naming the attachment point that enrolls them and the code that computes the sum.

Do the arithmetic rather than gesturing at it — n per group, what the estimator actually pools, what the imputed value literally is. This lens's authority is reconciliation, and a claim it cannot reconcile is not its claim to make.

Develop the subsidiary-cord and categorical-channel options far enough that they can be killed: storage, loader, reader, and the case each one cannot express (start with a symbol carried by twelve beings).
Treat readability as staffing: for every surviving option, name the keeper, the cadence, and what the archive looks like the day the keeper is gone.
task_context: Determine how the jawnomicon symbol tier should be structured: what vector (if any) a symbol entry carries, how symbols relate to the existing 29-axis eidogen space for beings, and where symbols sit in the graph and relatedness layers. Surface options beyond the four already listed, especially any that question whether a symbol should be a node with coordinates at all. Attack each option against the measured constraints: the five universal axes, the covariance ratchet's pairwise-deletion estimates, the hygiene-09 V-shrinkage lesson, the strict 29-key creature schema, and the downstream jawnsight grammar. Target document: docs/symbol-tier-design-question.md (jawnomicon-nhe.3).
